blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: When Respiratory Distress Hides a Pancreatic Leak
blogs.description: This post explores the cognitive bias of focusing on thoracic pathology in patients presenting with respiratory distress. We discuss the 'Pulmonary Mask' phenomenon where Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF) mimics primary lung disease, emphasizing the need to evaluate the abdomen even when chest symptoms dominate.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: The Diagnostic Anchor for Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: A deep dive into the diagnostic utility of pleural fluid analysis. We review the significance of markedly elevated amylase (>1000 U/L) and lipase levels as pathognomonic markers for PPF, and discuss the role of amylase isoenzyme typing to rule out salivary sources.

blogs.title: The Trauma Timebomb: Delayed Presentation of Blunt Abdominal Injury
blogs.description: Focusing on the case history, this post examines how blunt abdominal trauma can present weeks later with atypical symptoms. We discuss the challenges of eliciting trauma history in children, the mechanism of delayed pancreatic duct disruption, and the importance of revisiting the social history.

blogs.title: The TB Red Herring: Differentiating Infectious Effusions from Pancreatic Leaks
blogs.description: In endemic areas, tuberculosis is a common consideration for hemorrhagic effusions. This post analyzes the diagnostic tension between TB and PPF, specifically addressing how elevated Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) can mislead clinicians and why negative GeneXpert and high amylase are critical differentiators.

blogs.title: Medical Management of PPF: Octreotide, TPN, and Bowel Rest
blogs.description: An overview of the treatment algorithm for Pancreatopleural Fistula. We discuss the hierarchy of care, starting with conservative measures like nil per os, total parenteral nutrition, and somatostatin analogues (Octreotide) before escalating to endoscopic stenting or surgical intervention.

blogs.title: Pediatric Pancreatitis: Etiology and Epidemiology Differences from Adults
blogs.description: This post contrasts pediatric and adult pancreatitis. While alcohol dominates in adults, we highlight the prevalence of genetic mutations (PRSS1, SPINK1) and blunt trauma in children, discussing why PPF is rarer in the pediatric population and how this impacts diagnostic suspicion.
